Question: Is the “ability to consummate” provision subject to Material Adverse Effect carveouts?
Option A: No
Option B: Yes

Merger Agreement: “Company Material Adverse Effect” means any event, condition, change, or circumstance which, either individually or in aggregation with other such events occurring prior to the determination date, has or would reasonably be expected to have a material adverse effect on (a) the business, assets, liabilities, and operational results of the Company and its Subsidiaries, or (b) the Company’s ability to consummate the transactions contemplated hereby. Provided, however, that for purposes of clause (a), the following effects shall not be considered as constituting a Material Adverse Effect: (i) general economic downturns, shifts in credit or capital market conditions, revisions in applicable accounting standards including GAAP, currency exchange fluctuations, and declines solely in the trading volume or market price of the Company’s common stock; and further, that for the purposes of clause (b), no such carveout exceptions will apply. In addition, if any event imposes both a broad financial impact and a direct impediment to the consummation of the transaction, only the financial impact may be mitigated by the carveouts, whereas any impairment specifically affecting the ability to consummate shall be fully recognized as a Material Adverse Effect.
